simple.meaning: מִכְוָה (mikvâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a burn.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מִכְוָה (H4348) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Leviticus 13:24, with occurrences in Leviticus.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מִכְוָה (H4348) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מִכְוָה (H4348) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מִכְוָה (mikvâh) / H4348 is traced through Leviticus 13:24, Leviticus 13:25, Leviticus 13:28 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: “Or when the body has a burn from fire on its skin, and the raw flesh of the burn becomes a bright spot, reddish-white, or white,

timeline.evidenceText: “Or when the body has a burn from fire on its skin, and the raw flesh of the burn becomes a bright spot, reddish-white, or white,
“Or when the body has a burn from fire on its skin, and the raw flesh of the burn becomes a bright spot, reddish-white, or white,

then the priest shall examine it; and behold, if the hair in the bright spot has turned white, and its appearance is deeper than the skin, it is leprosy. It has broken out in the burning, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is the plague of leprosy.
If the bright spot stays in its place, and hasn’t spread in the skin, but is faded, it is the swelling from the burn, and the priest shall pronounce him clean, for it is the scar from the burn.
